newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - Shorter-dated FX vols march higher.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Shorter-dated FX vols march higher.

text.p: Implied volatilities for shorter-dated currency options continued firm on Monday after the dollar plummeted overnight to a fresh low against the yen.
"It has been very much a yen day," said a New York-based options broker.

One-month dollar/yen volatility pushed as high as 12.2 percent when the spot threatened 117.50 yen in Asian trading, traders said. It backed off to 11.0/11.3 percent by midday in the United States, compared with 9.6/9.85 Friday.
The explosion in volatility "shows there are quite a lot of shorts out there scrambling to cover," said a West Coast trader for a U.S. bank. "This is a shock to the market."

Fueling the momentum are Japanese exporters who had dollars to sell and have now jumped in to buy dollar puts to protect themselves, options traders said. At the same time, they said, U.S. interests see the spot at newly attractive levels and are purchasing dollar calls.
Both are contributing to the volatility run-up, which has caused a steep inversion in the curve, the U.S. bank trader said.
One-year dollar/yen implied volatility was 9.7/9.85 percent, firming from 9.45/9.65 Friday, but dropping behind one-month levels by about 1.5 point.
The dollar was recently bid at 118.85 yen and 1.7055 marks, with dollar/mark having rebounded after initially plunging in sympathy with dollar/yen.
"The speed with which it went back up created nervousness," said the options broker.
One-month dollar/mark climbed to 9.0/9.2 percent from 8.6/8.9 percent Friday.
Strong bidding on "anything short of one month" lifted volatility levels as market participants girded for more violent price swings and next week's Federal Open Market Committee meeting, he said.
One-year dollar/mark values declined, however, pulling back to 8.7/8.9 percent from 9.1/9.2 the previous session.
Mark/yen volatility leaped to 9.7/10.1 percent for one-month options, gaining 2.6 points from Friday.
One-month 25-delta risk reversals were favoring currency calls by 1.2/1.5 for dollar/yen and 0.3/0.6 for dollar/mark.
